children: NVIDIA fell about 13% for the week, closing at $166.19 on Nov. 12 after a 14% intraday drop. CFO Colette Kress became interim CEO as the board seeks a successor to Jensen Huang.
HSBC downgraded NVIDIA (NVDA) to Hold from Buy and cut its price target to $170 from $365, citing CEO succession uncertainty. Tighter export curbs could lower fiscal 2028 earnings estimates by 13%.
NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang was asked to testify to the Senate about export controls and Megaspeed’s access to its chips. NVDA fell nearly 11% for the week, then rose 1.2% in Friday premarket trading.
Bloomberg reported that servers with U.S.-restricted NVIDIA high-end chips reached a Shanghai data center via Megaspeed, after being sold to Singapore-based NVIDIA partner Aperia Cloud Services.
NVIDIA (NVDA) spent $42.4 billion on equity securities in the first half of fiscal 2027, up from $1.25 billion a year earlier. Its future customer-financing commitments drew scrutiny.
U.S. lawmakers seek tighter controls on China’s access to NVIDIA AI chips, including limits on remote rentals and new rules for Southeast Asia. Regional scrutiny could delay NVIDIA chip deliveries.
Michael Burry urged NVIDIA shareholders to sell, citing potential customer shifts to rival chips, order delays and renegotiations, plus risks tied to customer financing and supply commitments.
• NVIDIA Corporation (NVDA) and IREN announced a five-year, $3.4 billion cloud-computing contract and a strategic partnership.
NVIDIA (NVDA) has 12–24 months of order visibility, supporting revenue and earnings. Seaport warns customers may shift to AMD or custom chips, while limited capacity could curb earnings surprises.
NVIDIA invested $500 million in Corning, with warrants worth up to $3.2 billion more, to support three U.S. plants expected to boost fiber-optic output by over 50%.
